Compact a Parquet dataset into fewer, larger files

Source: R/pro_compact_parquet.R
pro_compact_parquet.Rd

pro_request_parquet() writes one Parquet file per API page (up to 200 records). That keeps the conversion parallel and resumable, but a large query becomes thousands of small files, which are slow to read. pro_compact_parquet() combines them into files of up to rows records. Records, columns and their order do not change.

Usage

pro_compact_parquet(parquet_dir, rows, verbose = TRUE)

Arguments

parquet_dir

Output directory of pro_request_parquet(), or the parquet folder of a pro_fetch() project.

rows

Maximum number of records per compacted file, e.g. 250000.

verbose

Logical. Report what was compacted. Default TRUE.

Value

parquet_dir (invisibly).

Details

Measured for 1.1 million works (5,460 page files): compaction took about 20 seconds; afterwards aggregates and lookups by ID ran 35 to 50 times faster, reading full records with DuckDB 4 times faster, and the dataset was 40% smaller. Files of 50,000 to 1 million records made no difference to read speed; rows = 250000 is a good choice (about 0.25 GB of full works records; newer works with abstracts and long reference lists are larger).

  • Each query's partition (query=<name>/) is compacted on its own; its _query.json and _query_oql.* files stay.

  • A compacted file holds whole consecutive pages, in download order, and is named after them: pages 1 to 1250 become results_pages_1-1250.parquet. A page with more than rows records becomes a file of its own. The page column is kept.

  • Files are compacted one at a time: each is written to a .part file, its record count checked, renamed, and only then are its pages deleted. If interrupted, run it again: it completes what was started.

  • Files compacted before are left as they are; only page files are combined.

  • If a partition cannot be compacted (for example because its pages have conflicting column types), a warning says so and its page files stay: the dataset is complete either way.

  • Indexes built by openalexSnapshot::build_corpus_index() or build_doi_index() point to files and row numbers, and would be wrong after compaction. If such an index exists next to parquet_dir, the function stops: delete the index, compact, and build it again.

See also

The compact_parquet argument of pro_request_parquet() and pro_fetch(), which compacts right after the conversion.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
pro_compact_parquet("my_project/parquet", rows = 250000)
} # }
